analysis.answer: Compared to current law, which has no specific rules regarding religious displays in classrooms, this measure explicitly requires all public school classrooms to display a poster of the Ten Commandments.

Direct costs include the expense of printing, framing, and distributing posters for every public school classroom in the jurisdiction. It also carries a highly probable opportunity and financial cost in the form of litigation expenses, as the state or districts will likely have to defend the mandate against constitutional challenges in court.

Civil liberties organizations and advocates for the separation of church and state are highly likely to file lawsuits seeking injunctions against the measure under the Establishment Clause of the First Amendment. Schools will have to determine how to source and fund the posters, potentially relying on private donations if public funds are not allocated.
As a statutory measure, it can be amended or repealed by the legislature, or struck down or enjoined by the courts if found to violate constitutional provisions.

flags.note: The text imposes a requirement on public schools to acquire and display posters without providing or identifying a funding source for them.

items.text: Expands religious expression in public institutions by requiring classrooms to display the Ten Commandments.
Reduces limits on government religious endorsement by mandating that public schools display a specific religious text.
